newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM call buying, put selling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM call buying, put selling.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp options were busy Friday, boosted by the November expiration and positive comments from Merrill Lynch, traders said.
"It's expiration day and it's very busy," said one trader in the IBM trading pit at the Chicago Board Options Exchange. "And Merrill raised its target on the stock."
At 1415 CST (2015 GMT), IBM shares were up 7-1/8 at 144, just a quarter point off its session high. Turnover was heavy at nearly 6.3 million shares.
The stock reached levels not seen since before the October 1987 stock market crash after Merrill Lynch raised its 12-month share price target to about $195.
The trader at the CBOE added that mutual funds had been active buyers throughout the week.
He said that on Friday, the IBM options activity was dominated by call buying and put selling.
The busiest IBM option was the expiring November 140 call, which traded nearly 9,300 contracts. With the stock surging, the option soared 3,500 percent, climbing 4-3/8 to 4-1/2.
The corresponding put option traded nearly 6,200 contracts. It tumbled 3-3/16 to 1/16 on its way to expiring worthless.
The November 135 call traded about 3,000 contracts and climbed 6-15/16 to nine.
In the December series, the December 145 call was most active, with 4,100 contracts changing hands. It rose 3-9/16 to five and had open interest of 1,507.
The December 140 put traded 3,930 contracts and lost 2-5/8 to 2-7/8. Its open interest was roughly 110. The January 140 and 145 calls were also busy.
